findings.summary: The Sentry Drone's two second roles are in the wrong order. Raider can only pass its coding rule through the gun that an upgrade adds, so it ranks at roles.secondary step 5 together with anti-infantry. Inside a step the roles list puts anti-infantry first, but the record has ['raider', 'anti-infantry'].
findings.evidence: Rules: data/vocab/roles.json says raider 'Needs a weapon that is not a tool (roles.primary step 2): a unit that harms nothing cannot hit and run'. That sentence has no 'As primary' in front of it. docs/fields.md roles.secondary says 'A role's coding rule binds here as for the primary, unless it says As primary.' Step 4 is 'Speed, armour or senses alone', and step 5 is 'Passengers, upgrades, doctrines, option weapons and acquired weapons ... A role that enters here may meet its requires through the part that gives it'. The same rule adds 'Inside a step, follow the order of the roles list.' In roles.json anti-infantry is item 2 and raider is item 11. Record: the stock drone is unarmed. Its only weapon, 'Sentry Drone Gun', has slot acquired, with the condition 'Added by the Sentry Drone Gun upgrade ... a stock drone is unarmed'. The record's own uncertain roles/secondary note says: 'Raider ranks at step 4 (very fast, light armour); its coding rule's need for a weapon that harms is met only by the upgrade gun. Anti-infantry ranks at step 5 from that gun.' Page: in the wiki infobox (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Sentry_drone) the weapon line is a 20mm gun, noted as there only after the upgrade. Compare the Overlord, where scout rests on an add-on and the batch ranked it at step 5, not by its stock parts.
findings.fix: Set roles.secondary to ['anti-infantry', 'raider']. Reword uncertain roles/secondary along these lines: 'Both rank at step 5, from the upgrade gun: raider's coding rule needs a weapon that harms, which only the gun gives, and anti-infantry comes from the tooltip's strong line on that gun. With one option each, the roles list puts anti-infantry first.'

verdict.reason: The rules as written do not decide this, and the batch already logged it as an open question for Mustafa. Rule problem item 45, 'A unit whose only weapon comes with an upgrade', sits under 'Open, for Mustafa' and says the rules do not say whether the upgrade gun can meet raider's need for a weapon at step 4 or only at step 5. Its proposed fix is exactly this finding's fix: put raider at step 5, after anti-infantry. That fix is a change to the field rules, not a data error. The finding builds its case on step 5's sentence 'A role that enters here may meet its requires through the part that gives it'. But that sentence covers a role's requires, and raider's requires (speed:>=fast) is met by the stock drone. The need for a weapon sits in raider's coding rule, and no rule says a coding rule met only by an upgrade part moves the role to step 5. Read strictly, the gun does not 'give' raider at step 5 either, because the rules say a weapon gives a role only when the weapon itself meets the role's requires. So a third reading would drop raider altogether. The Overlord comparison does not hold. There, step 4's own scout test (a sensor trait) comes only from the add-on: the Overlord's sensors.traits is empty, and the detector comes from the Gattling add-on. The drone's step 4 raider test (very fast, light armour) is met by its stock parts. The record's uncertain roles/secondary note gives the reading the coder took. No other unit in data/units has every weapon outside the stock slots, so no batch precedent goes against the record.
verdict.evidence: docs/fields.md line 42 (roles.secondary: the candidate definition, 'binds here as for the primary', steps 4 and 5, 'Inside a step'). data/vocab/roles.json, raider's source_rule and requires [speed:>=fast]. research/r3/rule-problems.md item 45 (around line 279, inside the 'Open, for Mustafa' section, lines 13 to 512): 'the rules do not say whether it may do so at step 4 or only at step 5', with the same fix proposed. The Overlord record: roles.secondary [scout, support], and its uncertain note says scout meets its requires only through the add-on's detector. A node scan of every data/units file found only the Sentry Drone with no weapon in the primary, secondary or alternate slots.
verdict.better_fix: No data change now. Leave the record as it is, with its uncertain note, until Mustafa answers rule problem item 45 in the rule-fix round. If he takes that item's fix, reorder to ['anti-infantry', 'raider'] then and reword the note.

findings.summary: The batch's own Iron Harvest Veterancy note says what to do when no source names a unit's veteran ability: code the buttons innate and add an uncertain entry at abilities. That entry must name the Veterancy page and the roles the choice would change. Anna Kos, Olga Morozova and William Mason code every button innate, and none of them has this entry. For Mason the choice matters: both of his second roles rest on one button.
findings.evidence: Rule: research/registry-notes/games-r3.md, Veterancy under Iron Harvest Game-wide mechanics: 'The first rank unlocks the unit's veteran ability ... Where no source names a unit's veteran ability, code its buttons innate, as the Ability sources tie-break says, and add an uncertain entry at abilities that names the Veterancy page and the roles the choice would change.' This text was added when research/r3/rule-problems.md item 89 was settled ('No unit changes'). Page: https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Veterancy says that reaching the first level, veteran, opens that unit's own veteran ability, a different one for each unit. I searched the cached Anna_Kos, Olga_Romanova and William_Mason pages for veteran, elite, rank and unlock: none names a veteran ability. Record: the ability sources are Anna [innate, innate, innate], Olga [innate x4] and Mason [innate x3]. None of their uncertain entries mentions the Veterancy page; the Mocny, Grimbart and Stark do have such an entry. Mason's uncertain roles/secondary note says 'Both at step 2. Anti-infantry from the revolver his Deploy Exosuit button switches to ... Area denial from the same button'. If Deploy Exosuit were his veteran ability, not every copy would have it, and area denial would rest on no step.
findings.fix: Add an uncertain entry at abilities to each of the three units. For Mason, for example: 'No source names his veteran ability. The Veterancy page (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Veterancy) says the first rank opens one for each unit, so his three buttons are coded innate by the Ability sources tie-break. If Deploy Exosuit is that ability, area denial drops and anti-infantry moves to step 3.' For Anna and Olga, write the same kind of note, naming the roles that would change: none for Anna; for Olga, scout if Camouflage is the veteran ability.

verdict.reason: Confirmed, judged by the letter of the registry note. The Iron Harvest Veterancy note says every unit ranks up, and heroes have four ranks. It then says the first rank unlocks the unit's veteran ability, and that where no source names it, the coder codes the buttons innate and adds an uncertain entry at abilities that names the Veterancy page and the roles the choice would change. Rule problem item 89 settled this text for the Mocny, the Grimbart and the Stark only, with 'No unit changes'. Nobody checked the heroes. Anna Kos, Olga Morozova and William Mason code every button innate, and none has such an entry: I checked every uncertain path on all three. No cached page for these heroes, their companions (Wojtek, Changa) or the other heroes names or flags a veteran ability. The coder of job j12 wrote the entry for the Stark but not for Mason. The choice matters for two of them. Mason's area denial rests only on the Deploy Exosuit button at step 2; his anti-infantry would fall back to step 3 through the cannon's splash. Olga's scout rests on Camouflage at step 4. There is one counterpoint, which the entry itself should record. KING Art describes hero ranks as health and damage bonuses (Change Log #04, 'Hero Veterancy', ranks I to IV). DevBlog #20 says standard units gain abilities at rank, while heroes level up skills in the campaigns. So heroes may have no veteran ability at all, but no source says so.
verdict.evidence: research/registry-notes/games-r3.md line 309 (the Veterancy note). research/r3/rule-problems.md item 89 (line 550). Cached iron-harvest.fandom.com pages: Veterancy (beta banner; two levels; the first unlocks the unit's ability), Ability, Hero (campaign skill points), and Anna_Kos, Olga_Romanova, William_Mason, Wojtek and Changa (no veteran, elite or unlock line about an ability). kingart-games.com/article/92 (Change Log #04: hero health and damage bonuses for ranks I to IV). article/67 (DevBlog #20: most units gain an ability or more; heroes level skills in the campaigns). article/117 (DevBlog #41: Olga's detonator is weaker before she ranks up). research/r3/fill/hesitations.md, j10 and j12: neither job raises a hero veteran ability.
verdict.better_fix: Add the uncertain entry at abilities on all three units, as proposed, but also name the evidence that cuts the other way: Change Log #04 describes hero ranks as health and damage bonuses, and DevBlog #20 sets heroes apart from standard units. For Olga, add that DevBlog #41 shows the detonator working before her first rank, so it cannot be her veteran ability. Only Camouflage, which carries scout, and Ride the Tiger, which carries no role, remain in doubt. For Mason: if Deploy Exosuit is his veteran ability, area denial drops and anti-infantry ranks at step 3 from the cannon's splash. For Anna, no role changes. The other option is a batch change to the Veterancy note itself, saying heroes are left out because their ranks give stat bonuses (Change Log #04). Either way, the note and the three records should agree.

findings.how: Fixed with the skeptic's fuller note: each of the three heroes has an uncertain entry at abilities that names the Veterancy page, the evidence the other way and the roles the choice would change.

findings.summary: countered_by/2 (damage:fire) does not describe something that beats the Thunderhead. It is about Penetrating weapons hurting the riders inside the Lightning Rod, which is a separate garrison building. The link also takes only half of the Penetrating list: it covers fire weapons and leaves out the Explosive - Penetrating ones. The entry is reasoned, but the uncertain note does not say so.
findings.evidence: Page: https://tempestrising.wiki.gg/wiki/Garrisoning describes the Penetrating passive as getting through garrisons, though not transports, and hurting the soldiers in them. It lists Explosive - Penetrating weapons (the Grenadier's grenades, the Scrambler's chaff, the Grenade Turret, the Cultivator's pods and the Shepherd's lightning) and Fire weapons (Ignitor, Pillager, Flame Turret). Record: countered_by/2 is 'damage:fire | Fire weapons with the Penetrating passive, such as the Ignitor's flamethrower and the Pillager's flame cannons, hurt infantry sheltering in garrisons such as its Lightning Rod (Garrisoning page).' Uncertain countered_by says only '...the third on the Garrisoning page, which lists the Penetrating weapons that hurt infantry inside garrisons'. Rules (docs/fields.md, Matchups): countered_by is 'What beats it; links describe the enemy'. 'A reasoned entry names those facts in its reason and gets an uncertain entry saying it is reasoned.' Rule (1): 'If that link alone drops half the point or covers units the reason is false for ... give that half a second entry.'
findings.fix: Remove countered_by/2. Put the point in weaknesses/0 (pattern:carry-passengers) instead, for example: '...and Penetrating weapons, fire and explosive alike, hurt the infantry inside the Rod (Garrisoning page).' Then shorten the uncertain countered_by note to cover the two entries that remain. If the entry is kept instead: add a damage:explosive entry for the Explosive - Penetrating half, and make the uncertain note say that both entries are reasoned.

verdict.reason: The main claim does not hold. The Lightning Rod is not a separate building: it is the Thunderhead's own deployable. The Rod page's Codex text has the Thunderhead put its core on the ground, and the Rod grows from it. The record's transport role, its ten seats and its strengths all rest on the Rod. Destroying the Rod kills everyone inside. Fire weapons threaten that garrison in two ways: Penetrating fire hurts the infantry inside, and the Rod is a Structure with no fire resistance, while the Damage page calls fire effective against structures. So the entry does name an enemy that beats the unit's main job. The batch also counts enemies that kill a carrier's riders in countered_by elsewhere: the Battle Bus's countered_by/2 covers crew-killing snipes and neutron shells that kill riders and crew. The 'half the list' point fails too. The reason is explicitly limited to fire weapons with the Penetrating passive, so it is not false. The other half has no fitting link: damage:explosive covers every weapon of the game's Explosive damage type, and the Garrisoning page lists only five of them as Penetrating. Rule (1) forbids a link that covers units the reason is false for, so the proposed alternative (adding a damage:explosive entry) would itself break the rules. That leaves whether the entry is 'reasoned'. That is a judgment call: the Garrisoning page states the Penetrating rule and lists the Lightning Rod among the garrisons it applies to, and the uncertain note cites that page. At worst this is a Low wording point, not a wrong link.
verdict.evidence: tempestrising.wiki.gg/wiki/Garrisoning (cached): Penetrating 'Breaches garrisons (but not transports)', the Rod listed with 10 units, five Explosive - Penetrating weapons and three Fire weapons. tempestrising.wiki.gg/wiki/Lightning_Rod (cached): armour type Structure, armorfire 0, armorexplosive 0; the Codex has the Thunderhead put its core on the ground; if the Rod is destroyed, everyone inside dies. tempestrising.wiki.gg/wiki/Damage: fire is effective against infantry and structures. data/games.json, the tempest-rising damage map: Explosive to explosive, Fire to fire. docs/fields.md line 11 (Matchups, rule 1). data/units/generals.json, the Battle Bus's countered_by/2.
verdict.better_fix: Keep countered_by/2 and do not add a damage:explosive entry. If a reviewer counts it as reasoned, add the word 'reasoned' to the uncertain countered_by note. Optionally, add to the reason that fire also hits the Rod itself at full strength (Rod page; Damage page).

findings.summary: The Engineers' strength calls them 'The cheapest unit in the game', and the cost basis repeats the wiki's claim. At the version researched that is wrong: by the batch's own registry prices, Saxon medics cost less than engineers.
findings.evidence: Record: strengths/4 is 'cost:very-low | The cheapest unit in the game and quick to train, by its page, so losing a squad costs little.' cost_band.basis says '...its page calls engineers the cheapest units in the game'. Page: the Pros on https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Polanian_Engineer include '* Cheapest units in the game'. That page's stat box dates from August 2019 and carries a beta banner. Registry (research/registry-notes/games-r3.md, Infantry prices): 'Engineers: 150 at the Headquarters and Barracks, 125 at the Advanced Barracks' and 'Saxon medics 100 and 75 (the wiki: 150)', taken from KING Art's later change logs. So Saxon medics are cheaper at both buildings.
findings.fix: Reword strengths/4: 'Among the cheapest units in the game, cheaper than the rifle squads, and quick to train, so losing a squad costs little (its page; prices in Change Log #17 and DevBlog #35).' In cost_band.basis, drop or qualify the 'cheapest units' clause (for example 'its page calls them the cheapest units, a line older than the medics' price cuts').

verdict.reason: Confirmed. The strength and the cost basis repeat the wiki's 'Cheapest units in the game'. That line dates from when engineers and medics both cost 150 iron. At the version researched, Saxon medics cost 100 at the Barracks and 75 at the Advanced Barracks (Change Log #17). Engineers cost 150 at the Headquarters and Barracks and 125 at the Advanced Barracks (Change Log #17, then DevBlog #35). DevBlog #35 raised the Advanced Barracks prices of engineers, riflemen, grenadiers and flamethrowers, but not of medics. No later post I could check changes either price: DevBlog #36 has no medic or engineer line, and the cached posts from Change Log #19 to DevBlog #47 list no medic or engineer price. Saxony does train medics (the registry's kit-only note). The registry's own price list agrees, so the record contradicts the batch's own figures. The very-low band itself stays right.
verdict.evidence: data/units/iron-harvest.json, iron-harvest.shared.engineer: strengths/4 and cost_band.basis. iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Polanian_Engineer (cached): beta banner, its Pros call engineers the cheapest units there are, costs_iron 150; the Saxon, Rusviet and Usonian engineer pages say the same, and the Polanian Medic infobox gives 150. kingart-games.com/article/106 (Change Log #17): Saxony medic 150 to 100 at the basic barracks and 100 to 75 at the Advanced Barracks; engineers 150 to 100 at the Advanced Barracks. article/107 (DevBlog #35): engineers 100 to 125, with no medic change. article/109 (DevBlog #36, fetched to the scratch folder): no medic or engineer line. research/registry-notes/games-r3.md lines 436 to 441: engineers 150 and 125, Saxon medics 100 and 75.
verdict.better_fix: Use the proposed rewording ('Among the cheapest units in the game, cheaper than the rifle squads, and quick to train...'). In cost_band.basis, qualify or drop the 'cheapest units' clause. Change Log #17 and DevBlog #35 are not among the engineer's five cited sources. If the reason cites them, add them to sources (supports strengths/4 and cost_band), or else put the price comparison in an uncertain entry marked read, not cited.

verdict.reason: Confirmed: the record contradicts itself. armament/2/summary says each attack order fires the rockets 'beside the cannon and machine guns', which has the side machine guns firing together with the cannon. crew.notes and the uncertain crew note keep the side machine guns with the driver because no source says they fire at the same moment as the cannon. Under the driver-gunner rule, such a weapon would go to the gunner. No source backs the summary's wording. The Kaiser page says only that the machine guns cover every side and fire on the move, and that Entrench raises damage output in all directions. The registry note says only that the Rockets fire with the attack order while the mode lasts. The record's as_player text (left mouse for the cannon, right mouse for the machine guns) matches the crew note, not the summary. The wording has stood since the reconciled opening-check entry.

findings.summary: The copy-check never compares anything with Steam news posts. It reads only Steam's page frame and none of the post. One fill agent (j07) reported this, but rule-problems.md and the R3 README leave it out. The README still says the online copy-check found no shared run in the 1173 pages it could read, and that count includes the Steam posts.
findings.evidence: htmlToText (copy-check.mjs lines 158-161) removes <head> and every tag together with its attributes. Run through it, each of the 25 cached Steam news pages (.cache/sources/store.steampowered.com/news_app_*) gives the same 155 words of page frame: the store's menu and footer words, the same on every page. The post text (630 to 6871 words per post) is only in the data-partnereventstore attribute, plus og:description in the head. The batch cites 22 different Steam news posts across its units, patterns, notes and record. All 9 Tempest Rising units cite them (17 citations). In fill/hesitations.md, j07's unclear rule 'Copy-check and Steam posts' says the official check 'passes trivially' and missed a real six-word run from the 1.6.0 notes. A grep of rule-problems.md for 'copy-check' or 'Steam posts' finds nothing, and the README's 'Copied wording' section does not mention it. I took the post text from data-partnereventstore and ran my own six-word check of the R3 units, all 69 pattern files, games-r3.md, patterns.md and research/r3 against it. It found only fragments of web addresses, so the data is clean today, but the check and the README claim are not.
findings.fix: In scripts/copy-check.mjs, for store.steampowered.com/news pages, build the page text from the data-partnereventstore attribute before making n-grams: decode the entities, JSON.parse, join the post-body strings, strip the [tags]. Add a test in tests/copy-check.test.mjs that uses one cached Steam page. Run the three copy-check parts again. In research/r3/README.md 'Copied wording', add that the 22 Steam posts were compared through this step, with the result. Add j07's item to rule-problems.md as a tooling problem, settled by the fix.

verdict.reason: Confirmed, with two corrections. The unit check reads only Steam's page frame. htmlToText (scripts/copy-check.mjs lines 158-163) drops <head> and every tag with its attributes, so each of the 25 cached news_app pages gives the same 155-word frame. All 9 Tempest Rising units cite 13 of these posts (17 citations), and each record is compared only with the pages it cites (lines 537-549). So no unit prose was ever compared with a post's text. j07's item is at research/r3/fill/hesitations.md:455. rule-problems.md and the README's Copied wording section do not mention it, and the README's 1173 pages include those 25 frame-only pages. Corrections: (1) 'never compares anything' overstates it. The two cached partner-events list pages (offset 0 and 100) hold the bodies of 112 posts, all 22 cited ones among them, and the --also step compares the notes with every cached page. So the notes were compared with the post text, apart from some JSON-escape noise. Only the units were not. (2) rule-problems.md covers word lists, field rules, the validator and the registry notes, and it lists no tooling items. Leaving this item out of it is defensible. The README and the runbook are where it belongs. The data is clean today: my own six-word check of every record and every R3 and registry note against the 25 post bodies and the 112 list bodies found 0 runs.
verdict.evidence: Ran htmlToText and words from copy-check.mjs over .cache/sources/store.steampowered.com/news_app_*: 25 pages, 1 distinct output of 155 words ('sign in store home ... report a translation problem'). The post text is only in data-partnereventstore and og:description. Two pages, the /view/ index and the coh3 post 1817483467037275, have an empty store. Post bodies run 38 to 4387 words for the Tempest Rising posts, not the stated 630 to 6871, but that does not matter. Ran node scripts/copy-check.mjs . --offline --also research/r3 --also research/registry-notes: 1173 pages checked, 36 not, 0 FOUND. Counted citations: 13 Tempest Rising posts in data/units, plus 9 more only in the notes = 22; patterns cite none. grep finds nothing in rule-problems.md or README lines 152-156; runbook section 8 step 4.3 names only PDFs and File: pages as blind spots. All 22 cited post ids are in the two cached events_ajaxgetpartnereventspageable pages. verdict.better_fix: In copy-check.mjs, for store.steampowered.com/news/app/ pages, build the text from data-partnereventstore: decode the entities, JSON.parse, join event_name, headline and body, strip the [tags], and add og:description. A page that yields no post text (an empty store, as on the cached /view/ index and coh3 post) should be listed as NOT CHECKED, not counted as checked. The test must use a small inline HTML fixture, because .cache/ is git-ignored and CI has no cached page. Re-run the three parts offline: the cached raw HTML already holds the posts, so nothing needs fetching. In the README's Copied wording section, say that the 22 posts were compared through this step (with the result), and that before it only the notes were compared, through the partner-events lists. Until the tool is fixed, add Steam news pages to runbook section 8 step 4 as a by-hand check, like the PDFs. Optionally add a caution to games-r3.md line 421. Record j07's item in the README rather than in rule-problems.md, which covers rules only.

findings.how: Fixed in the tool, as the skeptic's better fix asks: the copy-check reads a Steam post from the page's data attribute, lists a page with no post as not checked, and has tests with an inline page.
